question.question: Does Raft retain an effective automatic joint-exit continuation when applying an implicit joint configuration while leadership transfer blocks proposals, then aborting that transfer without changing leaders?
question.importance: A lost library-owned exit continuation can retain outgoing quorum requirements and prevent later configuration changes or reduce availability even after the transfer obstruction has ended.
contexts: No Byzantine messages; caller persists and applies ordered Ready work
Transfer message delivery can fail while a quorum remains responsive
No extra user proposal is assumed after admitted configuration change

question.trigger_rationale: The legal RawNode exploration reached applied=committed=last=3, retained AutoLeave, and cleared transfer by tick 10 while draining all Ready and message work. The next discriminator is exact repeatability of the post-abort suffix rather than extending its finite wait. Existing API assigns automatic exit to Raft and requires no unrelated proposal.

obligation.description: After a committed implicit joint configuration has been applied, Raft owns the continuation that proposes and completes exit when it is safe. A temporary leadership-transfer proposal obstruction must not leave a still-authoritative leader in a repeatable non-exiting execution after the transfer is aborted, while a quorum for both configurations is responsive and the caller continues the required tick, message, persistence and application work. No unrelated client proposal or manual leave-joint request is required to restart this automatic continuation.

excluded: No numeric exit deadline is asserted
No universal availability claim under missing quorum, unbounded transfer requests or missing caller work
Explicit joint mode assigns exit to application and is outside this obligation
Observed finite waiting alone is not a violation

grounding.derivation: The protobuf API expressly assigns implicit exit to Raft rather than the application and describes exit as automatic when safe. AppliedTo implements this by an internal zero-change proposal; proposal admission can reject it during transfer. TickHeartbeat bounds transfer obstruction but abortLeaderTransfer only clears the target. The applicable requirement is preservation of library-owned continuation under fair normal driving, not an invented tick deadline. A closed fair execution cycle that retains the implicit joint state would refute this responsibility.
grounding.applicability: Stable authoritative leader with both quorums able to acknowledge, after the admitted implicit configuration was applied and transfer aborted. All ordinary caller work continues; unrelated new proposals are outside required continuation.
unresolved: Formal execution and exact-cycle correspondence remain pending.
alternatives: New entry application or a new leader can restart exit; those conditional mechanisms remain counterevidence but are not owed by this caller schedule.

feedback.answered: The exploration completed a public RawNode history with implicit removal committed/applied at index 3 during transfer. The transfer case dropped one genuine TimeoutNow; by tick 10 transfer was cleared, while ticks 10/20/30/40 retained AutoLeave and last=committed=applied=applying=3 with empty driver/local queues, no unstable entries and no Ready. The no-transfer control exited at index 4. A separate normal proposal rescued the transfer case and exit applied at index 5. Thus pending ordinary Ready work did not explain the measured finite non-completion; later proposal-driven recovery remains confirmed as a conditional mechanism.
